{{nihongo|'''Ii Shrine'''|飯神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sanuki Province]].

'''Iii Shrine''' (いいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Marugame, Kagawa|Q460835|qid=Q460835}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|Q161454|qid=Q161454}}.

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}} {{ill|Utari district|Q11173974|qid=Q11173974}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}. The shrine stands on the southwestern foothills of {{ill|Mount Iino|Q11666715|qid=Q11666715}}, known as “{{ill|Seven Sanuki Fujis|Q11632541|qid=Q11632541|lt=Sanuki Fuji}},” and it is said that Mount Iino itself is regarded as a {{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}} <ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kagawa Prefecture Shrine Records, Vol. 2 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1227849/1/68?keyword=%E9%A3%AF%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE |website=dl.ndl.go.jp |access-date=2025-06-30 |publisher=National Diet Library |author=Kagawa Prefecture Association of Shinto Priests |editor=Kagawa Prefecture Association of Shinto Priests |language=ja |doi=10.11501/1227849}}</ref>.

=== Enshrined Deities ===
=== Principal deities ===
*{{ill|Iiyorihiko|Q65292980|qid=Q65292980}}
**The {{ill|Kunitama|Q9692242|qid=Q9692242|lt=land-tutelary deity}} of {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}. One of the aspects of {{ill|Shikoku|Q13991|qid=Q13991|lt=Iyo-no-Futana-shima}}. “Iii” is thought to mean “where grains gather,” suggesting a land abundant in food.
*{{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}}

=== History ===
* The founding date is unknown. It is said to have begun in prehistoric times when a group of rocks at the summit of {{ill|Mount Iino|Q11666715|qid=Q11666715}} were revered as an {{ill|Iwakura rock|Q11587880|qid=Q11587880}}. After being relocated to the mountainside of Mount Iino, it was moved to its present location in the first year of {{ill|Kōhō|Q1327182|qid=Q1327182}} ({{ill|964|Q23951|qid=Q23951}}) <ref name=":0" />.
* From the second year of {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten’an}} ({{ill|858|Q30371|qid=Q30371}}) to the sixth year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} ({{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}}), when {{ill|Kinonatsui|Q11605011|qid=Q11605011}} served as {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki kokushi}}, devotion to this shrine was strong, and it is said that annual {{ill|Hōhei|Q11445508|qid=Q11445508}} were made.
* From the second year of {{ill|Ninna|Q1346317|qid=Q1346317}} ({{ill|886|Q24683|qid=Q24683}}) to the sixth year of Ninna ({{ill|890|Q30481|qid=Q30481}}), {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} served as {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki kokushi}} and visited the shrine.
* On the 15th day of the 12th month of the fourth year of Ninna ({{ill|AD 888|Q29956|qid=Q29956}}), {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267}} granted the shrine the rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|Q11071125|qid=Q11071125|lt=Junior Fifth Rank Upper}} in the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} system.
* In the fifth year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it was listed in the “{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}” and received offerings from the state.
* In the ninth year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} ({{ill|1581|Q6717|qid=Q6717}}), the shrine was destroyed by fire during the military campaign of {{ill|Chōsokabe Motochika|ca|Chōsokabe Motochika|cs|Motočika Čósokabe|de|Chōsokabe Motochika|es|Chōsokabe Motochika|fa|چوسوکابه موتوچیکا|fi|Chōsokabe Motochika|fr|Chōsokabe Motochika|id|Chōsokabe Motochika|it|Chōsokabe Motochika|ja|長宗我部元親|ko|조소카베 모토치카|pt|Chokosabe Motochika|ru|Тёсокабэ Мототика|sk|Motočika Čósokabe|th|โชโซกาเบะ โมโตจิกะ|tr|Chōsokabe Motochika|uk|Тьосокабе Мототіка|vi|Chōsokabe Motochika|zh|長宗我部元親|zh_min_nan|Tyôsokabe Mototika|qid=Q1070082}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}.

=== Other ===
When {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} served as {{ill|Kokushi (official)|Q1351234|qid=Q1351234}} of {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}, he deeply revered Iii Shrine. It is said that when he returned to the capital, he carved a wooden statue and dedicated it to the shrine. The sacred object of the subsidiary Iitenn Shrine is believed to be that wooden statue <ref name=":0" />.
